newsitem.title: USA: White House calls tax cut issue "minor".
newsitem.headline: White House calls tax cut issue "minor".

text.p: White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles told reporters Friday that tax cut issues in the balanced budget proposal were "minor."
Bowles and Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin met with House Speaker Newt Gingrich to work out last-minute problems on reaching an accord to balance the budget and cut taxes through 2002.
Further meetings were being held during the day in the Capitol between House and Senate leaders and top White House officials.
A House Republican source said the current glitch in reaching an agreement involves the administration's request for increased domestic spending.
"If this thing falls apart, it's because the White House wants more spending," the source said.
The tax proposal would involve $135 billion in tax cuts over five years, partly offset by $50 billion in tax increases, including an extension of the airline ticket tax.
The tax portion of the budget would not specify tax cuts but would include a child credit, education credit, capital gains tax rate reduction and a new formula which would reduce the inheritance tax.
